defects.summary: No research/ module doc (module_core, module_tests) is updated for the new planner arm, the Kimi rows or the new test classes, but the knowledge-base rule makes this mandatory after every code change.
MustCarryNoFlags refuses Flags and Leading but not AddDirs, so a plan that carries --add-dir arguments is dropped silently, where decision 3 says a plan with ANY flag is refused.

S5.6.5 and S5.6.6 are put in a new class that copies RowFolder, RowTree, the Planned helper and the Kimi consultant factory from ConfinementPlannerTests, where the spec places them and Adapters() already builds the Kimi consultant.
Deviation 56 says the S5.5.3 test catches OperationCanceledException and does not say which ending it asserts, but the test asserts state failed and failureKind cancelled and catches nothing.

The 'refused' arm of S5.6.7 cannot fail on junction-first disposal, because no home or junction is made before the copy is refused, and there is no arm where the home is made and then the launch is refused.

W.summary: The planner arm, the rows, the vectors and the generated table are right, and all 12 scenarios pass with honest junction-first assertions. But AddDirs is not refused, the research docs are not updated, the S5.6.5/S5.6.6 helpers are copied into a new class, and one recorded deviation does not match its test.

defects.summary: It changes the user-visible Unconfined caveat for every runtime (C# and capabilityAdmission.ts) and the seed's 'unconfined' definition, which is outside E5.5/E5.6; no deviation records it, and RuntimeCapabilities.cs:14 still says 'a shell is always there'.
No research/ module doc is updated for the Kimi arm, the rows or the new tests, which the mandatory knowledge-base rule requires.
It removes the blank line between the Versions and Peak members, a stray whitespace change outside the feature.
Deviation 56 calls S5.6.7 'a Theory of three endings', but the test has four (it added launch-refused).
S5.5.3 does not check that the fake person's folder is intact after the cancelled check, which S5.5.2 and S5.6.7 do.

X.summary: The product code is correct (AddDirs included). The tests are strong: a launch-refused arm proves junction-first disposal of a home that was made, and Adapters() is reused through one Kimi factory. The ranking falls because of an unrecorded, out-of-scope rewrite of the shared caveat text and no knowledge-base update.

defects.summary: The 'refused' arm of S5.6.7 compares coai-question-* folders in the global temp directory before and after, which can fail if another test runs at the same time (the deviation admits it), and no arm covers a home that is made and then refused.

It declares its own OneShotFolder = "coai-vh" constant (also in AKimiQuestionRowTests) instead of VibeHomes.OneShotFolder, and it names two private properties _data and _temp with a field-style underscore.

The failing-turn arm of S5.5.2 asserts only that state is not 'answered', not that it is 'failed'; S5.5.1 checks only that the home is under coai-vh and named kh- with 13 characters, not the <8> segment.
The new Kimi() and PersonsPlaces helpers copy the Kimi entry of Adapters() instead of reusing it.
It adds the Kimi paragraph, but the flowchart in the same section still says '18 rows (6 runtimes × 3)'.

Y.summary: Correct and complete product code (AddDirs refused, both unknown-runtime lists updated). The best guard against vacuous tests: a positive KimiHome.AfterUnlink recorder proves a home was made and unlinked, and S5.6.6 is a Theory over Flags, Leading and AddDirs. Small duplication, one racy arm and a stale diagram keep it below Z.

defects.summary: The class does not have [Collection("fakecli-env")], which the model ConsultantCheckTests and the other three implementations put on their check tests, so it can run in parallel with tests that change the environment.
The new paragraph is dated 'E5.6, 2026-10-13', which is the measurement date, not the build date (2026-10-25).
S5.6.3 does not assert that the none plan's AddDirs and SnapshotSources are empty, and S5.6.6 tests only a Flags plan, although the code also refuses Leading and AddDirs.
It adds two seams (VersionExit and VersionHomesThere) where one Func, as in X, would do.

Z.summary: It meets every decision (AddDirs refused) and reuses Adapters() for S5.6.5/S5.6.6. Its S5.6.7 has an arm where the launch control refuses after the home and junction exist, and its S5.5.1 checks the exact <root>\coai-vh\<8>\kh-<10 hex> shape and the canary. It also updates module_core (diagram count included), module_runners and module_tests; only small test-isolation and doc-date defects remain.

reasoning: All four implementations have the same planner arm, rows, vectors and generated table, and all 12 scenarios pass, so the ranking comes from test strength, scope and the mandatory knowledge-base update. Z and Y update research/ and refuse any flag including AddDirs; Z goes above Y because of the launch-refused arm, exact J3 path checks and reuse of Adapters(), and Y wins on its positive unlink recorder but has a racy arm and copied constants. X tests well but makes an unrecorded change to the shared caveat text and skips the docs, and W has the same docs gap, does not refuse AddDirs, copies helpers into a new class and records one deviation that does not match its test.
